content.title: About
content.content: Multigrain Sun Chips are crunchy corn chips made from a blend of whole grains (wheat, corn, oats, rice) and lightly salted. They have a distinctive whole‑grain aroma and a mildly salty flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sun Chips were introduced in 1991 as the first multigrain snack chips in the United States.
The recipe uses whole grains rather than just corn starch, giving them a more nutritious profile than regular corn chips.
The product contains no artificial colors or flavors.
Various regional flavors exist, such as BBQ, Sour Cream & Onion, and Cheddar & Sour Cream.
Packaging is made from recyclable material, and Frito‑Lay works on reducing the product’s carbon footprint.

items.title: Higher whole‑grain content
items.content: Provides whole grains that are sources of dietary fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: Unlike some other snacks, Sun Chips are cooked without partially hydrogenated oils, reducing trans‑fat levels.

items.title: Fiber source
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Whole grains contain phenolic compounds with antioxidant activity.

items.title: Reduced sodium compared to regular chips
items.content: Salt content is generally lower than that of traditional potato chips.

items.title: Grain allergies
items.content: May contain traces of wheat, barley, or oats, which is important for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although moderate, individuals monitoring sodium intake should account for it.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Like most dry snacks, they are calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy multigrain chips as a standalone snack, crumble them over salads for crunch, use as a base for nachos, or dip them in guacamole, yogurt‑based sauces, or cheese dips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the original sealed bag or an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For extended freshness, store in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent staleness.
